critical_concepts.elaboration: The primary cause of most MIs. The fibrous cap of an atheroma breaks, exposing thrombogenic material.
Platelet aggregation and fibrin clot formation rapidly occlude the coronary artery.
Ischemia is reversible lack of oxygen; Infarction is irreversible tissue death.

interactive_questions.title: The Event Horizon
interactive_questions.prompt: Simulate the rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque and the resulting cascade.
interactive_questions.question: What is the immediate consequence of plaque rupture in a coronary artery?
interactive_questions.explanation: When the plaque ruptures, the exposed lipid core is highly thrombogenic. Platelets rush to the site, triggering the coagulation cascade, forming a clot that blocks blood flow in minutes.

theory.title: Atherothrombosis
theory.content:
A heart attack is rarely caused by the slow buildup of plaque alone. It is a sudden, cataclysmic event.

  1. Vulnerable Plaque: A lipid-rich core with a thin fibrous cap.
  2. Rupture: Stress tears the cap.
  3. Clot: Platelets adhere, activate, and aggregate. Fibrin mesh locks them in place.
  4. Occlusion: Blood flow stops. Muscle downstream begins to die.
theory.analogy: The Dam Burst. Atherosclerosis is the water level rising behind a dam (Plaque). A Heart Attack isn't just high water; it's the moment the dam wall cracks (Rupture). The rushing water and debris (Clot) instantly block the river downstream.
theory.application: This explains why aspirin (anti-platelet) is the first drug given. It stops the platelets from piling onto the dam break, preventing the clot from getting bigger.

critical_concepts.elaboration: Indicates transmural (full thickness) injury to the heart muscle. The hallmark of STEMI.
ST depression in leads opposite the area of injury.
Pathological Q waves indicate established necrosis (dead tissue).

interactive_questions.title: STEMI Localization
interactive_questions.prompt: Review the ECG leads. Identify the location of the infarction.
interactive_questions.question: ST Elevation is present in leads II, III, and aVF. Which wall of the heart is affected?
interactive_questions.explanation: Leads II, III, and aVF 'look' at the bottom (inferior) surface of the heart, which is usually supplied by the Right Coronary Artery (RCA).

theory.title: ECG Localization
theory.content:
The ECG is a map. Different leads look at the heart from different angles.

  • II, III, aVF: Inferior Wall (RCA).
  • V1, V2: Septal Wall (LAD).
  • V3, V4: Anterior Wall (LAD).
  • I, aVL, V5, V6: Lateral Wall (Circumflex).
theory.analogy: Security Cameras. The heart is a bank vault. The leads are cameras positioned on different walls. If Camera 2, 3, and aVF go dark (ST elevation), you know the break-in is happening at the South Entrance (Inferior wall).
theory.application: Inferior MIs (RCA) often affect the electrical nodes (SA/AV), causing slow heart rates (Bradycardia). Anterior MIs (LAD) affect the main pump, causing fluid in the lungs (Heart Failure).

critical_concepts.elaboration: Morphine, Oxygen, Nitrates, Aspirin (Historical mnemonic, though modern usage varies).
Restoring blood flow via PCI (Stent) or Fibrinolytics (Clot busters).
The time from ER arrival to inflation of the angioplasty balloon. Target < 90 mins.

interactive_questions.title: Code STEMI Protocol
interactive_questions.prompt: Prioritize your actions for a patient with active chest pain and ST Elevation.
interactive_questions.question: Select the immediate interventions.
interactive_questions.explanation: Aspirin (chewed) acts immediately on platelets. Nitroglycerin dilates vessels. Oxygen is used if hypoxic. The ultimate goal is the Cath Lab for PCI.

theory.title: Time is Muscle
theory.content:
Every minute a coronary artery remains blocked, more heart muscle dies permanently.

  • Anti-platelets (Aspirin/P2Y12): Stop clot growth.
  • Anticoagulants (Heparin): Stabilize the clot.
  • PCI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention): Mechanical opening of the artery with a balloon and stent.
theory.analogy: The clogged pipe. Meds are like pouring Drain-O down the sink—they help stop the clog from getting worse. PCI is calling the plumber to physically snake the drain and put in a new pipe (Stent).
theory.application: Oxygen is no longer given routinely to everyone, only if O2 sat is <90%. Too much oxygen can actually cause vasoconstriction!
